issue.description:
src/service/lifecycle.rs: update_issue (14-77), release_issue (80-111), close_issue (114-151), reopen_issue (154-185) all read the issue via get_issue_for_update and validate the --if-revision guard BEFORE starting the write transaction (conn.unchecked_transaction() at lines 65, 106, 146, 180), and the subsequent UPDATE statements match on 'WHERE id = ?' only, with no revision predicate (lines 319, 354, 416, 450 — each does revision = revision + 1 unconditionally).

TOCTOU: a concurrent process (multi-worker shared workspace is the supported model) can commit a change between the pre-transaction read and the write; the guard then passes against the stale revision and the update silently overwrites newer state — exactly the lost update README lines 128-130 promises fails with exit 4. The window is real for separate-process SQLite WAL connections; unchecked_transaction is deferred, so no write lock is held during validation.

Fix: perform the read + revision/lease validation INSIDE the transaction (and take it immediate so the snapshot cannot go stale before the write), or make each UPDATE conditional ('WHERE id = ? AND revision = ?') and map 0 affected rows to the existing conflict/exit-4 path.

Acceptance (run in repo):
1. New test with two connections to one workspace: conn A reads revision N; conn B performs an update (revision becomes N+1); conn A then runs a lifecycle op with --if-revision N and MUST get the conflict error (exit 4 semantics), not success.
2. Existing tests/r003_revision_guards.rs passes unchanged.
3. cargo test passes.
issue.notes: Fixed and shipped in 8492103. All four lifecycle ops now take the write transaction IMMEDIATE before reading the issue and validate the revision precondition + lease inside it; every UPDATE carries AND revision = ? with zero-rows-affected mapped to the existing Conflict/exit-4 path. New tests/r003_revision_guard_atomicity.rs (6 tests): a committed competing change makes each op at a stale --if-revision conflict with exit-4 semantics (incl. through the CLI), and the discriminating test races an uncommitted in-flight writer -- the guard waits for the write lock, re-reads, conflicts; the concurrent change survives untouched. Verification notes: (1) full cargo test run has 3 failures in cli_doctor (test_doctor_reports_open_issue_held_by_assignee, test_ready_frontier_emits_r001_reason_codes) and f017_forensic (test_f017_monolithic_checkpoint_basic) -- all three reproduce on pristine HEAD with this change stashed, i.e. pre-existing from the R035 commit ed4fb3d: the doctor message text drifted from what the tests assert ('Ready frontier warning'/'--clear-assignee' expected; doctor emits 'WARN ready_frontier: N open issue(s) are assigned and excluded...' with the remedy only in JSON details). Worth a follow-up bead. (2) Local test runs need a TMPDIR with no foreign .beads ancestor: /tmp/.beads appeared ~Aug 15 and breaks workspace discovery for every tempdir-based test; used TMPDIR=/var/tmp/bead-rs-tests. (3) cargo fmt/clippy: new and changed files clean; pre-existing fmt+clippy noise in doctor.rs/cli_doctor.rs/r035 tests left untouched.
issue.title: Enforce --if-revision atomically inside the lifecycle write transaction
